emma: Quick PRD intake draft for a 'model-tier fallback policy' feature — need fast review of problem/goals/non-goals/success metrics. paste below, pls comment with gaps or edge cases.

emma: PROBLEM: When model variants fail or capacity is constrained we currently route to higher-cost variants or remote regions without clear SLAs. Customers see unpredictable latency/cost and inconsistent outputs. Need a predictable, configurable fallback policy that balances quality, latency, and cost.

emma: GOALS:
- Deterministic policy engine that can be configured per-tenant/route.
- Explicit preference ordering for variants (latency-first, cost-first, quality-first).
- Automatic graceful degradation with observable SLOs and automatic fallback to cached responses when acceptable.
- Rollout controls: canary, percentage, and automatic rollback on quality regressions.

emma: NON-GOALS:
- Not aiming to train new models or change base model families.
- Not replacing long-term capacity planning; this is a request-time routing layer.

emma: SUCCESS METRICS (proposal):
- 95th percentile latency for fallbacks <= 2x baseline 95p for primary model.
- Cost delta from baseline <= 20% per tenant over a week (configurable).
- Quality regression measured by eval harness: <1.5% drop in key metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity depending on workload).
- Fallbacks triggered intentionally < 5% of requests for steady-state tenants.

emma: ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (draft):
```
- policy definitions stored in config service and exposed in API
- admin UI allows per-tenant policy selection and audit log of changes
- rollout supports canary (0-100%), rollback on quality/regression alert
- telemetry: per-policy metrics (latency, cost, quality, fallback count)
- automated tests + eval harness runs with synthetic traffic covering long contexts
- documented non-goals + migration guide
```

raj: engineering notes: add circuit-breaker for region failures and backoff windows. need a path for model-variant compatibility (tokenizer/format differences). also clarify: who owns default policy? product or infra?

sophia: ML: we must define exact eval suites per customer workload. one generic threshold won't cut it. propose `eval-profile` mapping per tenant and a canary eval job that runs on rollout traffic samples. also watch for hallucination drift when falling back.

yuri: design: for the console show a small policy simulator (enter sample prompt -> preview which variant would be chosen + estimated latency/cost). also add clear labels: "best-quality", "low-latency", "cost-saver" so PMs can select quickly.

matt: devex: expose SDK flags and CLI for temporarily forcing a fallback policy for testing. add a migration CLI to audit current implicit fallbacks. docs snippet should include `redwood fallback set --tenant T --policy cost-first`.

olivia-security: security: ensure fallback routing respects data residency and KMS boundaries. if a fallback would move data to a different region/environment we must block or require explicit opt-in. add an acceptance test for KMS key usage.

deploy-bot: INF-4512 created: "policy-engine: PRD intake + initial spike" link: https://tickets/redwood/INF-4512 :thumbsup:

emma: great feedback — I'll fold circuit-breaker, eval-profile mapping, and residency guardrails into the next draft. assigning owner for rollout simulator UI to @yuri, SDK flags to @matt, and infra spike to @raj. will post updated PRD by EOD Tue. thanks all :rocket:
